messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated KV cache reuse errors observed in serve-pool-3; /v1/generate 5xxs spiked. Incident ID 1870001111.
ryan: taking pager. brief me.
maya: joining shortly, travelling but on phone.
trent: looped in eng-runtime and eng-sre. OLIVIA you good to lead runtime?
olivia: on it. what are the failure modes?
ryan: client reports seeing garbled sequences and validation failures: 'kv_seq_mismatch' and 'unexpected seq offset'. 95/99th latencies up, errors ~10% on pool-3.
luis: traces show same KV key being returned for different requests. looks like when continuous-batcher merges requests, the kv_cache pointer is referenced instead of cloned. pointer aliasing.
jamie: stack snippet from host-21:
```
2026-03-14T14:02:12Z serve.runtime INFO reuse=true batch=3 ctx=ctx-x seq_req=88 seq_ret=12 
validation: seq_ret < seq_req -> seq_mismatch
```
olivia: that smells like the batch refactor where we optimized away some clones for perf. maybe new pooling combined with >1 batch size triggers alias.
ryan: mitigation options: A) disable continuous batching entirely B) flip kv_reuse flag to false C) roll back pool-size tweak D) run cache wipe on affected nodes. prefer quick config flip + cache wipe.
maya: I can flip flag via admin endpoint. will canary in us-west-2 first. command:
```
curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN\" https://console.redwood/api/admin/flags -d '{"serve.kv_reuse":false}'
```
deploy-bot: Flag rollout started -> target: serve-pool-us-west-2 (8 nodes). job=job-9002
maya: kicking off cache wipe on same nodes:
```
kubectl -n redwood run kv-wipe --image=redwood/kv-tools --command -- /bin/sh -c "./wipe --target=serve-pool-us-west-2 --pattern=kv_*"
```
trent: CSMs: notify customers in high priority list. avoid implementation detail; say we have elevated error rate affecting some gen calls and we are mitigating.
csm-anna: drafting status: 'We experienced an increase in failed generation requests for a subset of customers. Engineers have deployed mitigations and are monitoring. Some requests may see higher latency while mitigations are active.' Will post to status and DM top accounts.
luis: quick repro: run two parallel requests with different contexts, set batcher to immediate merge, assert kv_cache.owner pointer differs after clone. current code sets owner = shared_owner when batch>1; fix is owner = owner.clone_on_share(). Patch ready.
jamie: do we want to hotpatch binary? risk during incident. prefer config/flag approach then deploy correctness patch in next canary.
olivia: agreed. flip+wipe is lowest blast radius. we'll schedule binary fix tomorrow with tests.
maya: canary metrics: error rate dropped from 9.8% -> 0.6% on canary nodes; 95th latency back to baseline ~480ms. rolling to eu/east now.
deploy-bot: Rollout complete job=job-9002 status=success. All serve-pool nodes have serve.kv_reuse=false.
ryan: keep eyes on seq mismatch logs for 30m. collect traces for postmortem.
trent: assign postmortem leads: olivia (incident lead), luis (root cause + patch), jamie (tests + CI), maya (mitigation & rollout), ryan (IC), csm-anna (customer comms). deadline: postmortem draft in 48h.
olivia: checklist for postmortem: timeline, affected customers, reproduction test, code diff for clone-on-share, perf regression analysis with batcher off, rollout notes.
csm-anna: status updated. DMed top 12 customers, two replied asking for ETA; I've given ETA that fix will be rolled tomorrow and a permanent patch will be released after testing.
luis: creating PR with guarded clone-on-share and unit tests reproducing seq_offset regressions. PR link will be included in postmortem.
ryan: closing incident for paging; keep follow-up open P2 until PR merges and canary passes. thanks team. :heart:
incident-bot: Incident 1870001111 resolved by disabling KV reuse flag and cache flushes. Duration 00:41:22. Severity moved to P2 for follow-up work.
